answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust a river that only flows one way: a new identity starts with no privileges and must complete a long voyage of small, verified, paid tasks before reaching the haven of high-value work. Each step is attested on-chain by independent peers, so reputation is earned through real labor, not bought. A sybil attacker must pay the full voyage cost - time, fees, and completed work - for every fake identity, making mass fakery unprofitable.
